note: World reactivity: social interaction lines (greet follow-ups, antagonize/defuse) by voice and Standing band, and gossip/reactive barks picked from world state (src/systems/social.gd, gossip.gd). Original writing.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Mrs. Caddell. My wife says you're the best thing to come down that road since the mail.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Ma'am. If you're ever short of a dinner, ours is at six.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Passing through, or staying? Most folks can't decide either.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Fine day to be doing nothing in particular.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: I've got nothing worth taking, ma'am, so we can both save the trouble.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Mornin'. I'll just be going the other way.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: You're on the paper by the depot. I never saw you. I'm very nearsighted.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Lord. Don't stand so close, they'll think I'm with you.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Heard what you did for the Halvorsens. Buy you a drink sometime, if you drink.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: You're square, lady. I don't say that to many.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Hot work for October.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: You looking for hands? I can rope, shoe and lie about both.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: I know your kind. Mine's the same kind. Keep walking.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Whatever you want, I didn't see it.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Two hundred dollars, they say. I could use two hundred dollars. I'd rather keep my head.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Lady, half this town's counting what you're worth.

lines.speaker: lady
lines.line: Mrs. Caddell. The ladies' aid were talking about you. Kindly, for once.

lines.speaker: lady
lines.line: You've done more for this valley than the county ever did.

lines.speaker: lady
lines.line: You've the look of a woman who's ridden a long way.

lines.speaker: lady
lines.line: Good day. Mind the boardwalk, the third plank's loose.

lines.speaker: lady
lines.line: I'll thank you not to stop in front of my door.

lines.speaker: lady
lines.line: My husband's inside, and he's armed.

lines.speaker: lady
lines.line: Go on, before somebody fetches the sheriff. Not me. Somebody.

lines.speaker: lady
lines.line: I've children in the house. Please.

lines.speaker: lawman
lines.line: Ma'am. The sheriff says you're to be let be. I'm letting you be.

lines.speaker: lawman
lines.line: Quiet day, thanks to some folks.

lines.speaker: lawman
lines.line: Keep that iron holstered in town and we'll get along.

lines.speaker: lawman
lines.line: Ma'am. Town ordinance says no shooting inside the limits. Mostly it holds.

lines.speaker: lawman
lines.line: I've got my eye on you. Both of them.

lines.speaker: lawman
lines.line: Every time you ride in, I end up writing reports.

lines.speaker: lawman
lines.line: I know that face. Keep your hands where I can admire them.

lines.speaker: lawman
lines.line: You've got a lot of nerve, walking up to a badge.

lines.speaker: child
lines.line: Are you the lady from the newspaper? Can I see your gun? I won't touch it. Much.

lines.speaker: child
lines.line: Mama says you're a heroine. What's a heroine?

lines.speaker: child
lines.line: Is that your horse? What's her name? Does she bite?

lines.speaker: child
lines.line: I'm not supposed to talk to strangers. You're not very strange.

lines.speaker: child
lines.line: Mama says not to talk to you.

lines.speaker: child
lines.line: Are you an outlaw? You look like an outlaw.

lines.speaker: child
lines.line: You're on a poster! You look meaner on the poster.

lines.speaker: child
lines.line: I'm going to tell. No I'm not. Maybe.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: I beg your pardon? I'd heard you were a lady.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: That's uncalled for, Mrs. Caddell. I'll put it down to the heat.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: I've been insulted by better, and sober.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Mind your tongue, lady.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Say what you like. I won't give you a reason.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: I heard about you. I'll be on my way.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Didn't figure you for a mean drunk.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Lady, I'll let that one go on account of your reputation.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Say that again, slower.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: You looking for trouble, you've come to the right man.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: You don't scare me, Caddell. Much.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Big talk for somebody standing that close.

lines.speaker: lady
lines.line: Well! And I defended you at the sewing circle.

lines.speaker: lady
lines.line: There's no call for that.

lines.speaker: lady
lines.line: How dare you.

lines.speaker: lady
lines.line: I don't know where you were raised, but it wasn't in a house.

lines.speaker: lady
lines.line: Leave me be. Please.

lines.speaker: lady
lines.line: I'll scream. I've got good lungs.

lines.speaker: lawman
lines.line: That's a poor way to thank the law for leaving you alone.

lines.speaker: lawman
lines.line: Careful, ma'am. Respect's quicker lost than got.

lines.speaker: lawman
lines.line: Talk like that will get you a night in the cell.

lines.speaker: lawman
lines.line: I've arrested men for less.

lines.speaker: lawman
lines.line: Keep it up. I've been waiting for an excuse.

lines.speaker: lawman
lines.line: Go on. Give me a reason.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Hey! Keep your hands off me!

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: You've gone too far now.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Put your hands on me again and I'll put you in the trough.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: That's the last free one you get.

lines.speaker: lady
lines.line: Don't you touch me!

lines.speaker: lady
lines.line: Help! This woman's gone mad!

lines.speaker: lawman
lines.line: You just shoved a badge, lady. Last warning.

lines.speaker: lawman
lines.line: Hands off. Now.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: All right then. Let's settle it.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: You want it? You've got it.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Fill your hand, Caddell!

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: I've buried better than you!

lines.speaker: lawman
lines.line: That's it. You're coming in, one way or the other!

lines.speaker: lawman
lines.line: Draw, then, if that's how it is!

lines.speaker: lady
lines.line: Don't think I won't use it!

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: I want no part of you!

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Somebody fetch the sheriff!

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Ain't worth dying over!

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: You're crazy, lady!

lines.speaker: lady
lines.line: Somebody help!

lines.speaker: lady
lines.line: Stay away from me!

lines.speaker: lawman
lines.line: I'm getting the sheriff!

lines.speaker: child
lines.line: Mama!

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Well. All right. We'll say no more about it.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Apology accepted, Mrs. Caddell. I've had worse days too.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Fine. Just keep your distance.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Forget it. Too hot to fight.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Fine. But I'm watching you.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: All right. Just go.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: No harm done. I've said worse to my own brother.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Forget it, Caddell. Buy me a beer sometime.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Yeah, well. Watch yourself.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: I'll let it go. This time.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: You're lucky I'm a patient man.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Go on, then. Before I change my mind.

lines.speaker: lady
lines.line: I'll accept that. Barely.

lines.speaker: lady
lines.line: Very well. Good day.

lines.speaker: lawman
lines.line: All right, ma'am. Let's both pretend that didn't happen.

lines.speaker: lawman
lines.line: Fair enough. Holster your temper.

lines.speaker: lawman
lines.line: Fine. But I'll remember it.

lines.speaker: lawman
lines.line: Go and walk it off somewhere else.

lines.speaker: lawman
lines.line: One more and you're in irons.

lines.speaker: lawman
lines.line: Walk away. Slowly.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Too late for sorry!

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Sorry won't cover it!

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Talk's done, Caddell!

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: You should have thought of that before!

lines.speaker: lawman
lines.line: There's paper on you. Sorry don't tear it up.

lines.speaker: lawman
lines.line: You're coming in, sorry or not!

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Your hat's on crooked, and so's your face.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I've smelled better things on the bottom of a boot.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Do you practise looking that useless, or does it come natural?

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Move. You're standing in my light.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Get out of my road before I put you in the ditch.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: You're not worth the cartridge, but I've got plenty.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Out of my way.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I said move.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Go on. Push back.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Easy. I spoke out of turn.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I've had a long ride and a short temper. My apologies.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Let's leave it there. Nobody needs to bleed over words.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Put it away. I don't want to kill you, and I don't want you to try.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Heard a woman shot two syndicate men down by Willow Bend. Nobody's crying about it.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Somebody dug a grave on the hill last month and didn't put a name on it. That's not Christian.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: They tried to burn out that camp on the river. Didn't take. Hear they've a boy there now, a runaway.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Fenn's paper has a lady in it this week. Says she shoots like the Day of Judgment.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: That poster on the Lantern's door, the woman in the hat. They drew her from an old show bill, they say.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Somebody walked into the Linden Exchange at night and walked out again. The bank says nothing was taken. Banks always say that.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Shale's riders pulled down a windmill on the Halvorsen place. In daylight. That's how sure of themselves they are.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Ingrid Halvorsen's herd came through the Breaks to the Ybarra well. Thought she'd lose every head.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Ybarra well's gone bitter. Somebody threw a dead cow down it. The whole plaza smells of it.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: They tried to foul the Ybarra well, and somebody stood over it all night with a rifle. Water's still sweet.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Cutter Shale's in Mabry's cell. First time anybody's seen Mabry earn his pay.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: They buried Cutter Shale on the Dry Fork. Nobody came but the undertaker, and he charged double.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: First rain in four months, the night Cutter Shale went down. My mother would have called that a sign.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Garrity signed the miners' terms in Coldwater, they say. With a pistol in his ear. Won't hold, but it's a start.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: The territorial inspector's gone up to Coldwater to read Garrity's letters. First honest man up that road since the snow.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: They lit the powder on four men in Number Two at Coldwater. Company says it was an accident. Company says a lot.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: The westbound got stopped at Kessler's Tank. Some say it was the Shales. Some say it was worse.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Took the whole syndicate payroll off the express, I heard, and Pell's private book besides.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Pell's in print! Fenn ran his whole ledger, columns of it. My brother-in-law's name is in there twice.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: They walked Lucius Pell out of the railroad office in irons. He kept reaching for his hat.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Pell's building a new depot. Men like that never fall. They just get new offices.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Somebody robbed Pell's own office in broad day. Half the town cheered, and the other half counted the doors.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Eben Shale's waiting on the circuit judge in Bitter Spring. Reads his Bible to the jailer, they say.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Eben Shale's dead at San Lazaro. All three Shale brothers gone, or near enough.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: They found Eben Shale on his knees in the San Lazaro chapel. Whoever did it didn't wait for a judge.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: There's a man on the Greer road with a buggy that runs on steam. Frightened my mule into next week.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: My boy's reading a dime novel about a lady gunfighter. Miss Ruthie something. He's wearing my hat in the barn.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Folks up in Coldwater saw a light with a tail over the Kestrel one night. The old stargazer up there was right after all.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: The Lantern printed a map of a water line nobody's building. Funny how many syndicate men read it twice.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: The medicine show's packed off from Thornwood. Turns out the elixir was laudanum. My cousin hasn't stopped weeping.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Callahan boy's got a job at the Lantern now. Sweeps the press room, and tells everybody about his guardian angel.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Somebody poured the whole Silver Dollar into the mud at Coldwater. Grown men knelt in the street.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Somebody held up a store. The clerk says she had the calmest eyes he ever saw.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: That's three stores robbed now. Folks are keeping their money in their boots.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: A man was shot dead, and not by a lawman. Nobody's saying who, which says plenty.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: The road agents have gone quiet out on the plain. Something's been thinning them out.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: There's paper out on a woman. Rides a good horse and keeps her hat low. I'd keep my head down if I were her.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Things are quieter since that Caddell woman came. My wife lights a candle for her. I tell her that's Catholic.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Lock the door tonight. Caddell's in town.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Rain at last. Ingrid says it's too late for the grass and just in time for the mud.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Get indoors! Lightning took the top off the church steeple once. The Methodists never got over it.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Can't see the far side of the street. Good morning to be a thief.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Dust in the coffee, dust in the bed, dust in the Bible. The Lord made this country out of leftovers.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Not a cloud. My corn's praying for one.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Late to be walking. Only the saloon's still lit, and nothing good happens under that lamp.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Up before the roosters? Either you've work or a conscience.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Snow's early on the Kestrel this year. Miners will be eating their mules by Christmas.

lines.speaker: lawman
lines.line: I know that face. Walk on, slow, and we'll both live to supper.

lines.speaker: lawman
lines.line: Dead or alive, the paper says. I'm not choosy, Caddell.

lines.speaker: lawman
lines.line: Ma'am. Quiet day. Let's keep it that way.

lines.speaker: lawman
lines.line: One wrong move in my town and you'll be talking through bars.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: For you, Mrs. Caddell, the good coffee. Not what I sell the teamsters.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Look all you like. Touching's the same price as buying.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Cash on the counter first. Then we'll see what I've got.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: I've moved the till since last time. Don't ask where.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: If you've come back for the rest, there isn't any. You took it. Twice.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: They say Cole Hatcher came into town across a saddle. Alive, if you can call it that, and cussing.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Cole Hatcher's dead. The freight company sent a ham to the sheriff, which is the first thing they ever gave anybody.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: That false preacher, Ezra Penn, is in the county jail, preaching to the bedbugs.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Ezra Penn won't pass the plate again. Somebody settled his account with the Almighty direct.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Jinx Marlow's taken. Laughed all the way to the cell, they say.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Delia Fontaine won't be selling lavender water to widows any more. Thank the Lord for that.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Absalom Crow's done. The Kestrel miners drank to it in coin, not scrip.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Scotch McCready's finished singing. Somebody went up the Kestrel and brought him down.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Wade Pardee's been brought in. His brother Ivo's gone to Texas, which is where Pardees go to be forgotten.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Tobiah Rusk's paid for that deputy. The Wells put flowers on the boy's grave again.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Thackery swears somebody took the Grey Widow up on the Kestrel. The herders are lighting candles.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Old Ironhide's dead. The Thornwood cook got his sugar back and cried over it.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: The Pale Ghost is gone from the mission wall. The goat herders say the hills feel empty now.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Somebody finally took the Sable King. Fourteen points. Every hunter in the county is pretending he was there.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Eli Thackery at Greer's tells of a grey wolf the size of a pony. Buy him a drink and he'll tell you three more.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Somebody's been digging out at San Lazaro, they say, and came away heavier than they went.

lines.speaker: townsfolk
lines.line: Heard you sassed the deputy. Five-dollar mouth, my mother would have called that.
